selection.edition: international MaintainX REST API v1 (Composio MAINTAINX HTTP tools)
selection.ownership: MaintainX Inc (an Autodesk company), United States. The reviewed edition is the global API at api.getmaintainx.com, not a mainland-China product.

research.searchCoverage: Official MaintainX REST API v1 (HTTPS host https://api.getmaintainx.com/v1, Authorization Bearer, GET /locations, GET /locations/{id}, GET /workorders, GET /users, optional x-organization-id for multi-org tokens), MaintainX Inc / Autodesk US identity, and dated incident search (MaintainX + getmaintainx + security breach/incident) reviewed on 2026-09-13. No qualifying current unresolved MaintainX compromise was identified in reviewed coverage; this is not a breach-free claim.

Official MaintainX API documents HTTPS host https://api.getmaintainx.com/v1 and Authorization: Bearer. GET /locations (limit 1-200), GET /locations/{id}, GET /workorders, and GET /users were confirmed on 2026-09-13. Operator is MaintainX Inc (US; Autodesk company). Dated incident search found no qualifying current unresolved MaintainX compromise. Bounded coverage is not a breach-free claim.
research.waiverAuthority: User waiver dated 2026-09-13 permits historical non-China incident coverage.
research.qualityRationale: Read-only location, work-order, and user inventory with documented Bearer auth and cursor pagination bounds.

adaptations: Credential-only healthcheck maps to GET /locations?limit=1, matching the pinned validator.
Optional x-organization-id / x-organization-ids multi-org headers are omitted; single-organization tokens are the admitted path.
Native category is productivity: MaintainX is a CMMS/work-order product and there is no maintenance CATEGORIES value.
The upstream user-agent is not sent. Writes are omitted. Responses keep raw provider JSON under data.
Optional cursor and limit (1-200) use official query names. Pagination is caller controlled; nextPageUrl is returned as data and never followed.
id is a required positive integer path segment on GET /locations/{id}.
Optional cursor and limit (1-200) are admitted. Filter arrays (assets, statuses, expand, etc.) are omitted to keep the native query bounded and unused-input-free.
Optional cursor and limit (1-200) use official query names. Email/expand filters are omitted.
